title: Private Snafu: Spies
studio: Leon Schlesinger Productions (Warner Bros. Cartoons), dir. Chuck Jones, for the US Army Signal Corps (Army-Navy Screen Magazine); voice Mel Blanc
contents: Snafu gets drunk and blabs to a blonde spy; the secret travels through a hidden radio to Hitler, U-boats line up and torpedo Snafu's troopship. A wartime 'loose lips sink ships' lesson.
pd_us: US: PD. Wikipedia 'Private Snafu' > Availability: 'As now-declassified work of the United States government, all Private Snafu shorts are in the public domain.' Caveat on that wording: the shorts were made by a private contractor (Warner's Schlesinger unit underbid Disney; Seaman Tarfu was by Hugh Harman), and contractor work is not automatically a 17 USC 105 government work. They are PD anyway because the War Department released them as restricted training films without copyright notice or registration, which under the 1909 Act left them uncopyrighted. Disney made none of the Snafu shorts, so there is no Disney question.
pd_korea: Korea: PD. Korean Copyright Act Art. 42 protects cinematographic works for 70 years from publication (50 years before the 1 Jul 2013 amendment, which did not revive expired works); a film published in 1943 expired at the end of 2013 at the latest, so 1955-or-earlier films are PD. Korea's 1996 Berne restoration only covered foreign works still within the Korean term, so it does not apply.
trademark_caveat: None for Snafu. Contains Nazi swastikas, Hitler and 1940s caricatures (a wartime propaganda context); YouTube may limit ads or age-gate, so frame it as history.
audio: kept: original 1943 soundtrack (Mel Blanc, Carl Stalling score), AAC 160k mono
